diagnostics.description: Missing subcommand — e.g. bare `string` without a subcommand.
Too few arguments for command.
Too many arguments for command.
Shimmer parse error — internal representation cannot be determined.
Possible paste error — repeated assignment to same variable with same value.
Command invalid or ineffective in this iRules event.
Unknown iRules event name.
Deprecated iRules event.
`when` block missing explicit `priority`.
Data event without a matching `*::collect` call.
`*::payload` without a matching `*::collect` call.
`*::collect` without a matching `*::release` on the same connection side.
`*::release` without a matching `*::collect` on the same connection side.
HTTP command used after `HTTP::respond`/`HTTP::redirect`.
Multiple `HTTP::respond`/`HTTP::redirect` on different branches.
Deprecated `matchclass` — use `class match` instead.
Deprecated iRules command.
Unsafe iRules command.
Heavy `regexp` in a high-frequency event — consider `string match` or data-group.
Tainted data in HTTP response body.
Tainted data in HTTP header or cookie value.
Tainted data in `log` command — log injection risk.
`HTTP::uri`/`HTTP::path` set to value not provably starting with `/`.
`HTTP::path`/`HTTP::uri`/`HTTP::query` getter used without `-normalized`.
Write to `static::` variable outside `RULE_INIT`.
Generic `static::` variable name — collision likely across iRules.
Variable scoping concern across events.
Constant `set` in per-request event could be hoisted to an earlier once-per-connection event.
Potential race — `static::` variable written outside `RULE_INIT` and read in another event.
Ungated `log` in a high-frequency event.
`drop`/`reject`/`discard` without `event disable all` or `return`.
`DNS::return` without `return`.
Direct proc invocation without `call` — use `call proc_name`.
Single shimmer outside a loop — object internal representation changed.
Shimmer inside a loop body — per-iteration representation conversion cost.
Variable oscillates between two types across loop iterations.
Tainted data flows into a dangerous code-execution sink (`eval`, `expr`, `exec`, `uplevel`, `subst`).
Tainted data flows into an output command (`puts`).
Tainted data in option position without `--` terminator — option injection risk.
Unknown subcommand.
Command is disabled in active dialect profile.
Unbraced expression argument — prevents byte-compilation and risks double substitution.
`eval` with string concatenation — code injection risk.
`subst` on variable input — code injection risk.
`open` with pipeline `|` — command injection risk.
String concatenation for list building — use `lappend` instead.
Unbraced code block or missing `variable` declaration in `namespace eval`.
Dangerous unbraced `switch` body — risks double substitution.
Non-ASCII characters in token content.
Use `eq`/`ne` instead of `==`/`!=` for string comparison.
Line exceeds maximum length (see `tclLsp.style.lineLength`).
Trailing whitespace.
Procedure shadows built-in command.
Redundant nested `[expr]` — already in expression context.
Backslash-newline in comment silently swallows the next line.
Command used without a corresponding `package require`.
Subnet mask has non-contiguous bits.
Mistyped IPv4 address (octet > 255 or leading zero).
`exec` result not captured or binary format modifier requires newer Tcl.
Manual path concatenation — use `file join` instead.
Variable read before set.
Variable set but never used.
Variable substitution where name expected (`set $x`, `incr $x`, `info exists $x`, etc.).
Variable may not exist — use `unset -nocomplain` to suppress the error.
Unused proc parameter — argument is declared but never read in the procedure body.
Dead store — variable set but overwritten before use.
`source` with variable argument — code execution risk.
`uplevel` with string-built script — injection risk.
`catch` without result variable — errors are silently swallowed.
Regexp vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS).
Missing option terminator `--` on option-bearing commands.
Substitution in literal-expected argument position.
Non-literal command name — variable or command substitution as command.
`subst` without `-nocommands` — risk of unintended command execution.
`eval`/`uplevel` with `subst` — double substitution risk.

optimisations.description: Propagate constant variables into expressions and command arguments.
Fold constant integer expressions.
Fold constant `[expr {...}]` command substitutions.
Fold static procedure calls using interprocedural summaries.
Fold static string build chains into a single assignment.
Propagate constants into variable references and detect redundant computations (GVN/CSE).
Hoist loop-invariant computations.
Eliminate unreachable dead code.
Eliminate transitively dead code.
Eliminate dead stores.
Canonicalise expressions (InstCombine).
Brace expression performance hints (paired with W100).
Eliminate constant-condition compound statements.
Strength-reduce expressions (`x**2` → `x*x`, `x%8` → `x&7`).
Recognise `incr` idiom (`set x [expr {$x + N}]` → `incr x N`).
Remove redundant nested `[expr {...}]` in expression context.
Fold constant `[list a b c]` to literal value.
Simplify `[string length $s] == 0` → `$s eq ""`.
Fold constant `[lindex {a b c} 1]` to element.
Pack consecutive `set` literals into `lassign`/`foreach`.
Prefer `eq`/`ne` over `==`/`!=` for string comparisons.
Rewrite self-recursive tail calls to `tailcall`.
Convert fully tail-recursive proc to iterative `while` loop.
Detect non-tail recursion eligible for accumulator introduction (hint only).
Comment out unused procs in iRules (not called from any event).
Sink side-effect-free assignments into the deepest decision block (`if`/`switch`) that uses them.
Remove unused variable assignments — eliminate `set` statements for variables that are never read.
